chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Isa from Sa'id ibn Sa'd from Abul Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)
that he looked at a man and said to him: 'O Servant of God, make a will and prepare for that which is inevitable.' Exactly what he said happened, and he died three days after that.

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abul Hasan al-Rida (Imam Musa ibn Ja'far)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida advise a man to do before his death?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Imam’s *‘ilm al-ghayb* (knowledge of the unseen) regarding the specific timing of a companion's death, serving as a proof of his divine leadership (*Imamah*). The brevity of the man's life—dying just three days after the advice—underscores the certainty of death (*al-mawt al-muqarrar*) and the practical urgency of settling one's affairs, a key theme in Shia eschatological ethics.
